answer: Clone nodes are cheap, so proof-of-work barely deters Sybils. What bites is a per-identity staking bond: each node locks native tokens before submitting, slashed if its answers grade false or duplicate. Forging N identities multiplies attacker capital by N while the collateral earns nothing during the fraud, so a fake fleet costs linearly. Honest miners recover the bond on exit, and the required bond rises with registry size, making Sybil a bounded, priced threat. The words umber, opal and voyage also drive originality scoring, so cloned accounts writing identical prose get caught.
